title: I’m making an incremental brick-breaker called "Everbreak", and the Steam page is finally live
author: FormAdditional4097
selftext:
Hi everyone, as the title says, I’m making an incremental brick-breaker. I took an old game idea, simplified it as much as I could, and turned it into an incremental game. I’m working on the demo now.

You aim and shoot an orb to break blocks. Like other incremental games, you get upgrades and work your way through the zones, beating each zone’s boss block along the way.

I’ve been switching between Claude and Codex during development. The biggest help was moving an old project I’d coded by hand in Unity over to Godot. Doing it on my own would have meant spending quite a while learning a new engine and working through trial and error. The agent used the structure of the existing Unity project as a reference, and the migration went through without any major problems. And that was the point where I stopped writing the code myself(!!)

I’m not an artist, so I worked with an agent on the title artwork too. I didn’t use GPT 'imagegen' skill for it. I put together a rough draft and had the AI do the work in Photoshop. It was my first time giving art direction, and going back and forth with instructions for all the little details wasn’t easy. Since Astra came out, I’ve been seeing more people build workflows around 3D. I’d like to give that a try on my next project.

The demo still needs some work, but the Steam page is now up. Have a look if you’re interested, and if it looks like your kind of game, I’d appreciate a wishlist. Thank you!

[Everbreak on Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5094590/Everbreak/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aigamedev_first_post)
